public_rationale: TechCrunch’s February 7, 2025 headline reads: “DeepMind claims its AI performs better than International Mathematical Olympiad gold medalists” [e1]. This establishes the headline’s wording, but does not establish what DeepMind actually claimed or whether the performance comparison was true [e1]. Neither part of Marcus’s denial can be settled from this evidence [e1].
limitations: The packet contains no quoted DeepMind report or matched performance evidence.
The headline names IMO gold medalists but does not specify the task domain or whether it compares average or all gold medalists.
The embedded headline image in Marcus’s post could not be checked against the recovered headline.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The TechCrunch headline's claim about AlphaGeometry2 was not made by DeepMind and is not true.

statement.excerpt: DeepMind didn’t make that claim, and it isn’t true.
statement.document_title: AlphaGeometry2: Impressive accomplishment, but still a long path ahead

our_interpretation: Assess both the attribution to DeepMind and the truth of the headline’s performance claim.
A standalone reading suggests overall IMO performance. A reading informed by the article may restrict the comparison to geometry and average gold medalists.
The target is the February 2025 announcement discussed in the post, not subsequent systems.
criteria.support_condition: The contemporaneous headline makes a materially broader claim than DeepMind made, and evidence establishes that broader performance claim was false.
criteria.contradiction_condition: DeepMind explicitly made the same performance claim, or matching evidence establishes the headline’s claim under its intended scope.
